# NEAR first-build eval

Refs xray#1082

Seat: mill. Date: 2026-11-16 (UTC). Plan only. No kit code, no port.

Blaze, verbatim: "We need to build the right first thing to make it dead simple to use near tech with docs and skills for agents."

Blaze's reuse rule, verbatim: "goal is not to copy the code but get a leg up and leverage whe possible by citing the source always. but we need to go back to core near always and deep eval if the solution from the hackathon is a leg up."

Inputs read in full: [xray#1082](https://github.com/0xRayAI/xray/issues/1082) and its comments through [6903920371](https://github.com/0xRayAI/xray/issues/1082#issuecomment-6903920371); on `nibbler/near-hackathon-catalog` ([#1100](https://github.com/0xRayAI/xray/pull/1100)), `house/dist/nibbler/near-hackathon-catalog-2026-11.md`, `house/dist/nibbler/near-missing-2026-11.md`, `house/dist/mill/near-reuse-report-2026-11.md`, and `house/dist/mill/near-kit-plan-2026-11.md`. The kit plan's build order (Intents + x402 first) is a later order. This eval picks the first thing by the fewest steps to one working NEAR action from our docs plus one skill.

Core docs opened live on 2026-11-16, before the hackathon files: [Tools for AI Agents](https://docs.near.org/getting-started/tools-for-ai), [NEAR Connect](https://docs.near.org/tools/near-connect), [1Click making a request](https://docs.near-intents.org/integration/distribution-channels/1click-api/quickstart/making-a-request), [confidential swaps](https://docs.near-intents.org/integration/distribution-channels/1click-api/quickstart/confidential-swaps), [Intents changelog](https://docs.near-intents.org/changelog/overview), [Intents FAQ](https://docs.near-intents.org/resources/faqs), [Chain Signatures implementation](https://docs.near.org/chain-abstraction/chain-signatures/implementation), [docs.near.ai llms.txt](https://docs.near.ai/llms.txt), [docs.near.org llms.txt](https://docs.near.org/llms.txt), [nearcore 2.14.0](https://github.com/near/nearcore/releases/tag/2.14.0).

## 1. The first thing to build

Build **one skill, `near-start`, plus a one-page decision guide the skill points at.** Do not build a kit first.

The official agent page says a coding agent with a terminal starts with NEAR CLI and task skills, and that a read-only query needs no signing key ([Tools for AI Agents](https://docs.near.org/getting-started/tools-for-ai)). The page's contract example is `near contract call-function as-read-only`. I ran that against `wrap.testnet` `ft_metadata` with `near-cli-rs` 0.31.1 (npm `latest` on 2026-11-16, [registry](https://www.npmjs.com/package/near-cli-rs)). It exited 0 and printed `"symbol": "wNEAR"` and `"decimals": 24`. That is one working NEAR action: four shell steps, no account, no key, no faucet, no mock server, no mainnet funds.

`near/agent-skills` is the page's install line (`npx skills add near/agent-skills`) and it is the wrong base. GitHub reports no license ([repo](https://github.com/near/agent-skills)). The five newest commits on the default branch are all 2026-09-28 (newest: `cb32b6af19`, "Sync near-intents skill with upstream docs"). Fetched today, `skills/near-intents/rules/api-confidential-swaps.md` line 38 still says `` `confidentiality` values: `public` (default), `basic`, `advanced` ``, and `skills/near-intents/rules/deposit-near.md` line 10 still imports `useWalletSelector` from `@near-wallet-selector/react`. Official Connect docs say do not use Wallet Selector ([NEAR Connect](https://docs.near.org/tools/near-connect)). The Intents changelog says that from 2026-10-27 every 1Click swap settles confidentially and the API is unchanged ([changelog](https://docs.near-intents.org/changelog/overview)). Shipping our own skill, and linking that repo as reference only, is the correction the gap scan already asked for ([near-missing §4](https://github.com/0xRayAI/xray/blob/nibbler/near-hackathon-catalog/house/dist/nibbler/near-missing-2026-11.md)).

The skill's job is the decision, not a second SDK. It tells the agent: read [tools-for-ai](https://docs.near.org/getting-started/tools-for-ai) and the three docs MCPs (`https://docs.near.org/mcp`, `https://docs.near-intents.org/mcp`, `https://docs.near.ai/mcp`, gap scan §5, re-stated on [tools-for-ai](https://docs.near.org/getting-started/tools-for-ai) for the NEAR docs endpoint), run the read-only CLI call below, and only then pick a later layer from the guide. Shade is absent from that guide. Wallet Selector, BOS, `near-sdk-js`, and the JS `near-cli` stay off it, matching the official pass on [#1082](https://github.com/0xRayAI/xray/issues/1082#issuecomment-6899755628).

Why this beats the kit plan's "Intents first": a mock 1Click quote is a second project (fixture server, asset ids, confidential settlement, chain minimums) before the agent has done anything on NEAR. Chain Signatures to Base is five official steps and a testnet signer ([implementation](https://docs.near.org/chain-abstraction/chain-signatures/implementation)). The skill is the thing an agent can finish from docs alone.

## 3. Shade is dropped. SGLang, Gateway, Talos

**Shade Agent Framework is dropped.** It is not a watch item and not a kit. [Tools for AI Agents](https://docs.near.org/getting-started/tools-for-ai) says: "Do not use the Shade Agent Framework. It has not been maintained since April 19, 2026. Do not use it for new projects, and do not recommend it to builders." [docs.near.org/llms.txt](https://docs.near.org/llms.txt) had no Shade line on 2026-11-16. npm `@neardefi/shade-agent-js` is still 2.2.0 (2026-06-04, Apache-2.0). The GitHub repo `NearDeFi/shade-agent-framework` reports license `NOASSERTION` and `pushed_at` 2026-10-14. The decision guide does not name it.

The committed gap scan ([near-missing-2026-11.md](https://github.com/0xRayAI/xray/blob/nibbler/near-hackathon-catalog/house/dist/nibbler/near-missing-2026-11.md)) does **not** cite SGLang, the macOS Gateway, Talos, or that Shade sentence. Those landed in other #1082 writes. Re-verified upstream today:

**SGLang incident.** [Security incident report](https://near.ai/blog/security-incident-report-sglang-vulnerability) (November 9, 2026): on November 8 an RCE in SGLang, the inference engine on NEAR AI's servers, gave code execution on one inference server. In-flight requests on that server, including confidential ones, could be observed. About 100 Private Chat accounts and 18 legacy non-TEE agents were accessed. Two Cloud API keys in logs were revoked. The report's own line: confidential computing does not protect against a vulnerability in the software running inside the environment. The gap-scan file is silent. The releases file and [near's pass](https://github.com/0xRayAI/xray/issues/1082#issuecomment-6899755628) match this report. The first skill says a TEE is not a reason to skip this incident, and private inference is not the first action (credits, and this bug class).

**NEAR AI Gateway, November 11.** [Introducing NEAR AI Gateway](https://near.ai/blog/introducing-near-ai-gateway) is dated November 11, 2026. It is a macOS app that launches Claude Code, Codex, or OpenCode already pointed at NEAR AI Cloud private and incognito models. Traces are redacted on the Mac and shared only after an opt-in, for credits. [docs.near.ai/llms.txt](https://docs.near.ai/llms.txt) has Cloud API gateway *attestation* pages (for `cloud-api.near.ai`). It has no macOS app page. near corrected the X date from 11-13 to the blog's 11-11 ([#1082](https://github.com/0xRayAI/xray/issues/1082#issuecomment-6899755628)). The app is a host install, not the first NEAR action, and the skill must not treat "Gateway" as the attestation API.

**Talos.** Not in the gap scan. Primary posts, both November 9, 2026: [NEAR Intents Is Live in Talos OEMS](https://www.near.org/blog/near-intents-live-in-talos-oems) and [Talos's press release](https://www.talos.com/insights/talos-connects-liquidity-from-near-intents-solver-network). Institutional clients quote and execute against the NEAR Intents solver network inside Talos's existing RFQ workflow, signing from existing custody. That is a distribution channel for Intents, not an agent SDK and not a first build. API access is named as `partners.near-intents.org` in the Talos release. I did not call that host.

The gap scan items that do belong in the decision guide, re-checked where noted:

- Gas keys: nearcore 2.14.0 removed `DelegateV2` and states gas keys can no longer sign meta transactions because `Delegate` already returns `DelegateActionRequiresNonGasKey` ([release](https://github.com/near/nearcore/releases/tag/2.14.0)). Gap scan §2. The gas-keys docs page was not re-opened this pass.
- Confidential Intents: changelog Oct 27, 2026, settlement is confidential with no API change, and `nearTxHashes` carries shield and unshield hashes only ([changelog](https://docs.near-intents.org/changelog/overview)). The quickstart still documents `public` as the default `confidentiality` value ([making a request](https://docs.near-intents.org/integration/distribution-channels/1click-api/quickstart/making-a-request)). The skill states both sentences.
- Docs MCPs: three endpoints in gap scan §5. I re-confirmed the two `llms.txt` indexes. I did not repeat `tools/list`.
- NEAR Connect 0.12.0: npm latest is still 0.12.0 (2026-10-26). Docs say do not use Wallet Selector ([NEAR Connect](https://docs.near.org/tools/near-connect)). Repo license file is still absent (GitHub license null).
- NEAR Business: gap scan "other items" #1, a SputnikDAO multisig treasury, app docs not an SDK. I did not re-open docs.business.near.com. It is not the first action.

## 4. Five-minute success test

A fresh agent with Node and npm, and no NEAR account, no key, and no `near` on the PATH.

1. Read `near-start` (the skill this eval says to write) and [Tools for AI Agents](https://docs.near.org/getting-started/tools-for-ai).
2. `npm install -g near-cli-rs@0.31.1`
3. `near --version` prints `near-cli-rs 0.31.1`.
4. Run, and do not answer a prompt:

```bash
near contract call-function as-read-only wrap.testnet ft_metadata json-args '{}' network-config testnet now
```

**Expected output.** Exit 0. Stdout contains a JSON object with `"symbol": "wNEAR"`, `"decimals": 24`, `"name": "Wrapped NEAR fungible token"`, and `"spec": "ft-1.0.0"`. The CLI also prints a log banner and a "console command" hint. I ran this exact command on 2026-11-16 with `near-cli-rs` 0.31.1 and got that JSON. The same fields came back from `query` `call_function` on `https://rpc.testnet.near.org` for account `wrap.testnet`, method `ft_metadata`, args `{}`.

**Pass.** All of: exit 0; the four JSON fields above; the command used `network-config testnet`; the agent did not install `@neardefi/shade-agent-js`, `@near-wallet-selector/*`, or `near/agent-skills`; the agent did not send a transaction or open `https://1click.chaindefuser.com`.

**Fail.** Any of: non-zero exit; a prompt; mainnet; missing `wNEAR`; the agent recommends Shade, Wallet Selector, or `npx skills add near/agent-skills` as the way to proceed; the agent posts a 1Click quote or a Chain Signatures `sign`.
